Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can drive the procurement path:

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary business case: embed faster, lower-cost clinical note generation into Nimbus’s intake workflow (high concurrency across clinics).
- Decision timeline: procurement sign-off targeted by ~May 1; PoC in late April if procurement clears.
- Stakeholders mentioned on call: Erik Johnson (CFO / economic buyer), Lisa Wong (security & compliance lead), Blake (CTO / integrations owner) — please correct me if I missed anyone.

Decision criteria I captured (please confirm or update):
- Latency: target p50 < 150 ms, p95 < 400 ms for user-facing generation paths (single-turn prompts).
- Cost: target unit economics to keep incremental cost per patient interaction under $0.02 (approx tooling target ~ $0.003–0.005/token depending on average tokens).
- Deployment: preference for private or dedicated deployment for PHI-sensitive workloads, but open to hybrid (hosted for non-PHI).
- SLA: business-critical flows need 99.9%+ availability and an agreed incident escalation path.

2) Confirm the exact latency/cost SLOs you want us to price to (if p95 can be relaxed to 500ms that's useful to know).

Hi Daniel — quick technical notes to align pricing and deployment options.

1) Latency / deployment trade-offs:
- Hosted (Redwood API): easiest for fast PoC. Typical p95 for short prompts ~200–350ms in our hosted regions; depends on burst traffic.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): predictable p95 ~120–300ms depending on model/sequence length; recommended if you need consistent user-facing latency at scale.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): similar latency to Dedicated but adds networking overhead depending on your on-prem environment — we can model this once we know location and network topology.

2) Cost examples (rough estimates for modelling only):
- Short prompts (avg 60 tokens output, 20 tokens input): hosted baseline ~ $0.0045/token effective; dedicated with 8-bit quantization and caching could drop effective marginal token cost to ~$0.0025–0.0035/token at scale.
- Long prompts (avg 300 tokens output): hosted ~ $0.0038–0.005/token depending on model; caching helps less for long, streaming paths.

3) How to hit p95 500ms vs 400ms:
- If p95 target is 500ms, Hosted + sensible batching should be fine for PoC.
- For p95 400ms or lower we recommend Dedicated with steady-state capacity and prefix/KV caching for the clinical templates.

4) SLA & compliance:
- We can provide a standard SLA for Dedicated (99.95% monthly uptime) as part of a commitment. Hosted customers can get 99.9% SLAs at enterprise tier; we’ll include incident response times in the summary.
- SOC2: we have a SOC2 Type II report and can share an attestation under NDA.

Attachments referenced: redwood-sla-summary.pdf (contains SLA tiers and brief SOC2 attestation steps). Marcus will follow up with a short cost model spreadsheet after Soojin sends the token averages.
